cover.title: Workspace
p3s1i0: A screen that manages the workspaces across the whole system. A workspace is a container for projects and the unit of user assignment, so to start a study, first create a workspace here.
p3s2i0: Open it from Workspace management in the left menu.
p3s2i1: Create new workspace — Creates a new workspace 1.2.
p3s2i2: Summary — the total, active and inactive workspace counts, the total number of projects, and the total number of member assignments.
p3s2i3: Search and filter — find workspaces by name or code, and narrow them by status and lead organization.
p3s2i4: The subtitle states the scope of this screen — system-wide viewing, creation and deactivation.
p3s2i5: Status cards — show first what needs attention, such as the distribution by organization, active workspaces with no members assigned, and active workspaces with no projects.
p3s2i6: The table shows name, code, lead organization, number of projects, number of users, status and last entered. Select a name to go to its details 2.1.
p3s2i7: The ⋯ at the right end of each row has View details · Assign users · Deactivate (for an inactive workspace, Activate). This menu is shown only to system administrators.
p3s3i0: Only system administrators can create or deactivate workspaces. Workspace administrators can only view the workspaces assigned to them.
p3s3i1: Workspace administrators do not see the ⋯ menu at the right end of each row at all. It is not that the items are just disabled; the column is empty, so open details and user assignment by selecting the name directly 2.1 · 3.1.
p4.title: Create new workspace
p4s1i0: Creates a new workspace. The three items marked with an asterisk must be filled in. After creation, you go straight to the details screen.
p4.cap.1: Create window opened above the list
p4s2i0: Workspace name — The name shown to users. You can change it later 2.2.
p4s2i1: Code — A unique code that identifies the workspace. As the label notes, it cannot be changed after creation, so decide it carefully.
p4s2i2: Lead organization — Select the organization that leads this workspace. If it is not in the list, register it first in Organization management.
p4s2i4: Description — Optional. Writing what kind of study the workspace holds makes it easier to tell workspaces apart in the list.
p4s2i5: Selecting outside the window or selecting Close discards your input.
p4s3i0: The code cannot be changed after creation. Check your organization's code rules before you enter it.

sec2.3.title: Users · activity · deletion
p5s1i0: Shows all the information and to-dos for a single workspace together. You can see at a glance how far setup has progressed and what to do next.
p5.cap.1: Workspace details (SCR-WS-004) — the list of projects under it continues below
p5s2i0: Edit name and description — Edits the name and description 2.2.
p5s2i1: Shortcut — Goes to the screen of the step shown as Next to-do.
p5s2i2: Create project — Creates a project in this workspace 3.3.
p5s2i3: User assignment management — Manages the workspace members 3.1.
p5s2i4: Deactivate workspace — Changes the status to inactive.
p5s2i5: The header shows the name, active status, code, lead organization, creation date and time, and the description.
p5s2i6: Setup progress — Four steps: create workspace → assign users → create project → operation. Selecting each step card also takes you to that screen.
p5s2i7: Summary — the total and active project counts, the total number of subjects, and the number of assigned users.
p5s3i0: Even if the number of active projects is 0, there may still be projects overall. Projects in the setup stage (Setting up) are not counted as active.
p6.title: Edit name and description
p6s1i0: Edits the name and description. It does not move to a separate screen. The header card of the details screen switches to input mode in place.
p6.cap.1: Edit name and description — the header card switches to input mode
p6s2i1: Description — Edits the description of the workspace.
p6s2i3: Cancel — Discards your changes and returns to view mode.
p6s2i4: The Code field has “(Cannot be changed)” added to its label, has a grey background and cannot be selected.
p6s3i0: If you change the name, it is reflected immediately on the screens of all users who use this workspace. If the workspace is in operation, notify the members of the change.
p7.title: Users · activity · deletion
p7s1i0: The bottom of the details screen has a member summary, an activity log and a deletion area. Deletion has strict conditions, so usually use deactivation instead.
p7.cap.1: Bottom of the details screen — assigned user summary · recent activity · deletion area
p7s2i0: View all — Goes to the screen where you manage all the assigned users 3.1.
p7s2i1: Delete workspace — Cannot be selected unless the conditions are met.
p7s2i2: Assigned users is a summary, so only up to 5 people are shown.
p7s2i3: Recent activity — Changes made in this workspace are listed from newest to oldest. You can see who changed what and when.
p7s2i4: When deletion is blocked, the reason is shown. The screenshot is a case where deactivation has not been done first.
p7s3i0: Deletion is possible only when the workspace is inactive and all of its projects are in the setup stage or there are none. Deletion permanently removes the workspace and everything under it, so it cannot be undone. Do not delete a workspace that has been in operation. Deactivate it instead.

p8s1i0: A screen for assigning users to a workspace and removing them. Only users assigned here can take part in the projects of this workspace, so do this before assigning project roles.
p8.cap.1: User assignment management (SCR-WS-003) — workspace member list
p8s2i0: Add user — Assigns a user to the workspace.
p8s2i1: Change history — Looks up the records of assignments and removals.
p8s2i2: Designate as administrator — Promotes that user to workspace administrator.
p8s2i3: Remove — Removes the user's assignment from the workspace.
p8s2i4: You can return to the higher-level screen from the path shown at the top.
p8s2i5: The Role column is the user's position inside the workspace (member or administrator). It is separate from the role inside a project (such as researcher or monitor).
p8s3.name: Other ways to reach this screen
p8s3i0: Workspace management list → ⋯ at the right end of the row → Assign users (system administrators only)
p8s3i2: Workspace details → the 2. Assign users step card in Setup progress
p8s3i3: Workspace details → View all in the assigned user summary
p8s3i4: Workspace dashboard → the same three places as above 3.2
p8s3i5: Researcher assignment screen in a project → the link shown when members are insufficient
p8s4i0: If you remove a user from the workspace, that user's project roles are also cut off. Check whether the user has work in progress before you remove them.
p9.title: Workspace dashboard
p9s1i0: The screen you move to from the Operation step of Setup progress, and also the screen every role lands on when entering the workspace. It has almost the same layout as the details screen on the administrator path, but the range shown depends on the viewer's permissions.
p9s2i0: Shortcuts · Edit name and description · Summary are the same as on the details screen 2.1.
p9s2i1: Create project — The same button as on the details screen 3.3.
p9s2i2: User assignment management — The same button as on the details screen 3.1.
p9s2i3: View change history — Cannot be selected without permission.
p9s2i4: The path begins with Workspace ›, which differs from the Workspace management / of the administrator path. Check here which one you are in.
p9s2i5: Setup progress is shown collapsed. Selecting it expands the four steps.
p9s2i6: There is a search for projects in this workspace, and the number of participating organizations is shown in a column.
p9s3.name: Other ways to reach this screen
p9s3i0: Select a workspace in the workspace list
p9s3i1: Continue (recently entered) or My projects on the platform home
p9s3i2: Select a workspace in the context switcher at the top of the screen
p9s3i4: The guide screen you pass through when switching workspaces
p9s3i5: Workspace details → the 4. Operation step in Setup progress, or Shortcut
p9s4i0: What you see depends on your permissions. Regular members cannot see the member list, Setup progress or recent activity, so do not judge that the screen looks different as an error.
p10.title: Create new project
p10s1i0: Creates a project inside the workspace. A project is created with the Setting up status, and after setup is complete, you move it to the operation status.
p10.cap.1: Create new project — the Create button stays disabled until the required fields are filled
p10s2i0: Project code — A unique code that identifies the project. As the label notes, it cannot be changed after creation.
p10s2i1: Project name — The name shown to users.
p10s2i2: Study type — Select from options such as investigator-led.
p10s2i3: Retention policy — Sets how long data is kept. The default is Standard.
p10s2i4: Create project — Stays disabled until all the required fields are filled.
p10s2i5: The header shows the target workspace and the initial status.
p10s2i6: The usable characters and the length limit are shown below the code field.
p10s2i7: Initial roles — Do not select any. When you create a project, the standard roles are generated automatically by the system.
p10s3.name: Other ways to reach this screen
p10s3i0: Workspace details or dashboard → Create project button
p10s3i1: Workspace details or dashboard → 3. Create project step card in Setup progress
p10s3i2: The guide button shown in the project list area when the workspace has no projects
p10s4i0: You cannot create a project in an inactive workspace. The relevant step and buttons in Setup progress are all locked.
p11.title: Access to inactive workspace
p11s1i0: When you try to enter an inactive workspace, the content is not shown and only a notice remains. This is not an incorrect access. It means that workspace is inactive.
p11.cap.1: Attempt to enter an inactive workspace
p11s2i0: Retry — Loads the page again. Use it after the workspace has been reactivated.
p11s2i1: The notice “This workspace is in an inactive state.” is shown. The notice replaces the whole screen, so the list and summary are not visible.
p11s3i0: Deactivation can be reversed. A system administrator can reactivate the workspace from the ⋯ menu on its row in the Workspace management list, and it is restored right away 1.1.
